pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/query.rs:1522 The structural guard against `Utc::now().date_naive()` reads query.rs only up to the FIRST #[cfg(test)] (line 949), so the executable grants route code at lines 1015-1269 (list_fits, grants_for_profile, create_grant_profile) is outside its haystack, and the forbidden expression put back there would pass the guard.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/query.rs:1522 Comments and test code are rightly stripped from the haystack, but the population is cut at the first of four test modules, so ~250 lines of route code are silently excluded while the doc comment claims 'everything above the test module'.

crates/server/src/routes/query.rs:1538 The 'seeded violation' appends the forbidden text and then checks that the string contains it. That cannot fail, and it never runs the guard in count_and_page_cannot_select_different_sets, so the guard has never been seen going red.

crates/server/src/routes/search.rs:520 The degraded-index decision is lifted into the pure index_degraded_reason (search.rs:134) and asserted directly. Its single call site is search.rs:157; adoption is not asserted in this file.
